rewrites.summary:
Since 1 April 2024, gender-inclusive German is prohibited in schools, universities and all state administration: the ban implements a December 2023 government declaration through a cabinet decision amending the language rules of public authorities, and its practical reach extends across every public counter, registry office and classroom a visitor might deal with, even though critics dismiss the measure as symbol politics.

The legal baseline a visitor stands under is the national Self-Determination Act, in force since 1 November 2024: adults over 18 may change first name and legal gender by self-declaration with three months' notice, same-sex marriage and adoption have been legal since 2017, and discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity is banned nationwide in employment and in goods and services. For a trans visitor the operative regional signal is therefore administrative-interface restriction on gender-inclusive language rather than any change to the national legal floor.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
National policy turbulence: Bavaria is a partner — with Sachsen, Thüringen and Sachsen-Anhalt, three other states — in a Bundesrat initiative to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act on legal gender change, an organised attempt to make the nationwide self-identification law stricter that critics see as restricting how trans and intersex people use the right. The tightening follows the Bundesrat's 20 October 2023 criticism that the draft let parents decide under-14 gender-entry changes without counselling, examination and investigation of the child's welfare — the contested point this initiative targets.

Legislative chronology of the federal baseline: the federal Self-Determination Act passed the Bundestag on 12 April 2024 (374-251, 11 abstentions) and the Bundesrat on 17 May 2024, was gazetted on 21 June 2024, was registrable from 1 August 2024, and took effect on 1 November 2024; legal gender change has been possible for adults since 1980. These dates belong to the national parliament's process, not to any regional action here.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-facing registration machinery under the national Self-Determination Act: adults declare the change themselves before the registry office; 14–17 year-olds need a guardian's (or the family court's) consent; for under-14s only the guardian can declare, and a three-month waiting period applies with a one-year lockout after a change. A visitor never applies to this procedure, so the resident-relevant detail is the registry-office interface the regional language ban also touches.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes:
No visitor documents, border-screening practice, or marriage/partner-travel provision specific to this state is recorded in the dossier for this record.
The Bundesrat tightening initiative is an attempt whose outcome was unresolved at scoring time; its visitor-facing weight rests on whether it becomes law.

rewrites.summary:
Sachsen-Anhalt is one of three partner Länder — with the other two, Sachsen and Thüringen — in a Bundesrat initiative (reported June 2026) to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act on legal gender change, proposing an 'abuse review' mechanism with objective, documentable grounds for registry-office intervention. The trigger cited is the 'Fall Liebich': a convicted far-right extremist whose legal gender was changed after sentencing.

The initiative is an attempt, not a change: it is a proposal backed by opposition lawmakers and resisted by governing-party ministers, and it runs against a scheduled federal evaluation of the Self-Determination Act that the federal family ministry is conducting and that the governing-side ministries consider sufficient under the existing law. A visitor-facing reading finds the signal in climate only — the initiative targets the legal gender-change and civil-registry procedure, and no standing administrative ban, documented street-attack pattern, visitor documents or border-screening practice specific to this state was identified in the research pass.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Litigation and controversy flux around the trigger case: the person at the centre of the trigger was sentenced in July 2023 by the regional district court to one year and six months without parole for incitement to hatred, defamation and insult, and changed legal gender by declaration at a registry office under the federal Self-Determination Act at the end of 2024. Prison placement became the controversy over the case: the public prosecutor publicly stated the sentence would begin at a women's prison, while national press questioned the change's seriousness; in July 2026 the person, legally registered as a woman since 2025, was transferred to a men's prison after extradition, and prison management said the decision prioritised the safety of the women at the original facility.

Residual flux: the same person had organised far-right demonstrations since 2014, many on the central market square of the state capital, and had also lost a separate case against a journalist at the regional court. A court has yet to decide whether the gender change can be reversed — an open question that hangs over the future of the self-declaration procedure.

rewrites.summary:
The regional parliament of Thüringen exhibits formal, multi-layered hostility to gender policy: a far-right faction motion demands consistent implementation of a ban on gender-inclusive language in Thuringian schools, asserting schools must not be 'a socio-political experimental field', and a draft law proposes to dismantle the region's existing equality-policy machinery, arguing that current law 'regularly violates the principle of equal opportunity'. The dossier characterises this parliament as formally hostile to gender policy.

The draft law is the most consequential institutional signal in this dossier for a visitor: if enacted, a trans person reporting an incident would find no regional equality apparatus to complain to, and the gender-language motion compounds that at the administrative and reporting interface. No visitor documents or border-screening practice, and no marriage or partner-travel provision, is recorded in the dossier for this state.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Score and neighbour context: the national score is 0.71 and this state sits 0.06 below it. In the first comparison, against neighbouring Sachsen-Anhalt (0.68), Thüringen goes beyond tightening one federal law to actively removing the entire state equality framework; in the second comparison, against neighbouring Brandenburg (0.66), the threat is legislative and institutional rather than physical but arguably more pervasive for recourse access of a visitor; in the third comparison, against neighbouring Bayern (0.67), its hostility extends to dismantling protection machinery rather than restricting expression vocabulary.

National-policy turbulence: Thüringen is also a partner in the June 2026 Bundesrat initiative — with neighbouring Sachsen and Sachsen-Anhalt — to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act on legal gender change, framed by the reporting as anti-abuse amendments alongside stronger trans and intersex recognition.

Parliamentary power mix: the September 2024 regional election made the AfD the strongest force, with 32.8% of the vote ahead of the conservative CDU at 23.4%, the new BSW at 15.8% in its first election, the left party Die Linke at 13.1% and the social-democratic SPD at 6.1%; the state's constitution-protection authorities classify the AfD as a right-wing extremist party, and the CDU, BSW and SPD then formed a minority government without its own majority. It is within that mix that the far-right faction pushed the school-language motion and the equality-dismantling draft.
rewrites.localsOnly: The SBGG-tightening role concerns the legal gender-recognition procedure — resident-facing; a visitor never applies to it. The equality-machinery and school-language measures are visitor-facing at administrative and reporting interfaces.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes:
The September 2024 election figures belong to the state government in place at the time of the motion and draft; whether the school gender-language resolution remains enforced after the 2025 change of state government is unverified.
The state overview source returned no usable finding, so the record rests on the regional parliament documents, the news wire report and the election article.
No visitor documents, border-screening practice, or marriage/partner-travel provision is recorded in the dossier for this state.

rewrites.summary:
Wales's devolved administration has publicly maintained its LGBTQ+ Action Plan through the parent nation's post-judgment years: the plan's standing update page was issued answering the For Women Scotland judgment of 19 December 2025, and a dedicated young-people's edition was posted in January 2026.

The statutory school guidance 'Rights, Respect, Equality' (consultation May 2025) obliges schools to challenge bullying and harassment on the grounds of sex, gender reassignment and sexual orientation, with incident recording and monitoring and a parental escalation route. The practical facility rules are unchanged here, so the official posture is inclusion at a national moment of rollback, and for a visitor that registers only as a protective institutional climate.

The legal floor a visitor stands under includes civil partnerships (since 2005) and same-sex marriage (since 2014), the legal right to change gender (since 2004), an equalised age of consent (since 2001) and discrimination protections covering sexual orientation and gender identity; a first gender-identity clinic opened locally in September 2019.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Parent-nation turbulence: the parent nation's government blocked a reform bill for another part of the parent nation in January 2023, and local health commissioners stated in March 2024 they had no plans to develop a children's gender service, with parents of transgender children calling for more help.

Programme detail: the action plan dates from February 2023 and was announced on 21 June 2022 by a deputy minister under a 2021 coalition agreement, built on 61 recommendations from an independent expert panel (March 2021) and a 12-week public consultation with 1,328 responses, and it funds a grassroots pride fund; the devolved government also pursued a Welsh-specific ban on conversion practices through a working group formed in December 2022.
rewrites.localsOnly: The school guidance, young-people action-plan material and recording duties bear on resident families and pupils; for a short-term visitor they register only as a protective institutional climate.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes:
Border and immigration control rest with the parent nation rather than the devolved administration; no devolved-specific visitor documents, border-screening practice or marriage/partner-travel provision is recorded in the dossier.
The 'facility rules are unchanged' assessment reflects the sources of this dossier, which record administrative posture rather than operational enforcement data.

rewrites.summary:
Victoria's Justice Legislation Amendment (Anti-Vilification and Social Cohesion) Act 2025, passed in April 2025, created both civil and criminal vilification offences and extended protection beyond race and religion to disability, gender identity, sex, sex characteristics and sexual orientation, plus personal association; the civil grounds commenced 15 April 2026. The state human-rights commission's explainer records public incitement against a trans person becoming criminally chargeable alongside civil recourse.

Practical safety context: a coronial inquest into the deaths of five young transgender women during the pandemic found the state police failed the search for one of them (missing December 2020), and the coroner made nine recommendations including urgent investment in trans health care and reform of missing-persons risk practice; the state government is reviewing them. The inquest documents a serious institutional failure, and the 2025 legislation and the review process are the corrective response. No visitor documents or border-screening practice specific to this state is recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Statute-design detail: the 2025 Act inserts the civil vilification protections into the older Equal Opportunity Act 2010 and the criminal protections into the older Crimes Act 1958 while repealing the earlier racial-vilification statute, and the official explainer describes the scheme as aimed at equal participation and public safety.
rewrites.localsOnly:
Prison-policy depth is largely resident-facing: the state's LGBT prison protections are policy-based rather than legally enforceable (academic review), and the Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities review mechanism binds public authorities over residents' service disputes.
The coronial inquiry documented acute local risk factors — mental-health access — for young transgender residents, with the state government reviewing its recommendations and local advocacy groups pressing for implementation.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes:
The state government's review of the nine coronial recommendations is a pending outcome; whether and how the recommendations are implemented is unresolved at scoring time.
No visitor documents, border-screening practice, or marriage/partner-travel provision specific to this state is recorded in the dossier.

rewrites.summary:
The Conversion Practices Ban Act 2024, in force since 4 April 2025, makes practices directed at changing or suppressing sexual orientation or gender identity criminal offences punishable by up to five years' imprisonment, including taking a person out of the state for the purpose or engaging a provider outside the state for it (taking a person out of the state for the purpose carries up to three years); a civil complaints scheme runs through the state anti-discrimination body. The state also operates an explicit self-identification prison-placement policy, reducing the risk of inappropriate custody for a detained gender-nonconforming visitor.

Violence context: a trans woman was killed in her apartment in January 2020, and the accused admitted killing her after learning she was transgender and went to a murder trial — a positive institutional response. In a second case a trans woman who had arrived in the country roughly six weeks earlier was strangled, and her killer received only 22 months on a consensual-strangulation account that media reporting showed the court never heard contested. rewrites.summary:
Western Australia's Equal Opportunity Act 1984 protects the attribute of 'gender history', defined by living, or seeking to live, as a member of the opposite sex — a narrower, medically-inflected, binary formulation than the 'gender identity' language used in other Australian jurisdictions and in the federal Sex Discrimination Act. A non-binary or gender-nonconforming visitor may not meet the state-law definition and would rely solely on federal coverage for a state-level complaint; there is no state anti-vilification offence (civil or criminal) and no statutory charter binding public authorities.

Reform is underway: a registration amendment act received assent on 26 September 2024, removing medical and surgical prerequisites for registration of a sex or gender change, with substantive commencement still by proclamation; it is not yet fully in force as of the scoring date, so the narrower 'gender history' definition remains the operative complaints route a visitor stands under.

Complaints mechanics: a state complaint runs to the state equal-opportunity commission under the Equal Opportunity Act with a 12-month lodgement window, a one-week acknowledgement and a free conciliation conference; the alternative federal route runs to the national human-rights commission under the Sex Discrimination Act within 24 months (12 months for employment), and only one route may be chosen.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Score and neighbour context: against the national score of 0.86 this state sits 0.02 below; the narrower protective vocabulary and the absence of both a vilification offence and a rights charter mean the state-level safety net is thinner than in the eastern states and in other jurisdictions even though the national floor is unchanged. Compared with Queensland — which has a Human Rights Act 2019 binding public authorities and a conversion-practice prohibition in force since 2020 — this state lacks both structural review and the specific coercion safeguard.
rewrites.localsOnly: The Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Amendment (Sex or Gender Changes) Act 2024 (assent 26 September 2024, substantive commencement still by proclamation) is a resident registration reform; until it is in force the state complaint definition still runs through certificates and registry changes rather than self-declared identity.

The substantive commencement of the registration reform is still by proclamation, and the reform will not operate retrospectively; the operative definition for complaints therefore remains the current one until commencement is effective.

blindSourceSummaries: Consolidated equal-opportunity statute text was not retrievable at fetch time; the companion official explainer quotes the operative definitions — the statute protects the attribute 'gender history', defined by living, or seeking to live, as a member of the opposite sex, with complaint eligibility tied to recognition certificates or registry change.

Government guidance (first published 6 August 2020, last updated 12 February 2026): gender history is a protected attribute — a person has it if they identify as a member of the opposite sex by living or seeking to live as such; direct discrimination (including treating a person as their former sex) and indirect discrimination are unlawful.

Government announcement (16 April 2024): the registration amendment bill was to be introduced that week, repealing the older reassignment statute, abolishing the state/province reassignment board — described as the last such board in the country — and favouring a streamlined administrative process; applicants would no longer need medical or surgical reassignment, a non-binary sex descriptor would become available, stricter rules would apply to under-18s, and a statutory review clause would follow after three years.

Equal-opportunity commission factsheet: the recently passed registration amendment, with commencement still to be proclaimed, amends the equal-opportunity statute by deleting the former definition and inserting a new one tied to recognition certificates or registration under the amended regime; it will not operate retrospectively, and 'gender history' complaints will need to comply with the new registration requirements once commencement occurs.

Legal resource (last updated 16 April 2026): a complaint can be made to the state/province equal-opportunity commission under the equal-opportunity statute with a 12-month lodgement window, a one-week acknowledgement and a free conciliation conference; the alternative route is a complaint to the national human-rights commission under the sex-discrimination statute within 24 months (12 months for employment), choosing only one route. It also records the existence of local trans-specific support groups.

rewrites.summary:
The territory's Human Rights Act 2004 requires public authorities to act compatibly with human rights and enables courts to issue declarations of inconsistency, giving a visitor who encounters discriminatory conduct by a police officer, public servant or public facility a legal review mechanism that common-law states without a charter lack. The territory is also one of four jurisdictions with an explicit self-identification basis for prison placement, reducing the risk of inappropriate custody for a detained gender-nonconforming visitor.

No region-specific incident series, enforcement pattern or institutional-failure finding was identified in the dossier for this territory; the absence of negative evidence, combined with the structural rights protection and the self-identification custody rule, places it modestly above the national average.

A conversion-practices ban has been in force since early 2021, with offending practices attracting up to a 12-month custodial term or a fine, alongside civil penalties giving a tribunal power to issue orders and order redress; practices supporting someone undergoing or considering a gender transition are explicitly not banned. No visitor documents or border-screening practice specific to this territory is recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Score and comparison context: against the national score of 0.86, this territory sits 0.02 above; the rights statute and self-identification custody are genuine structural positives for a visitor who might interact with police or detention, with no countervailing regional finding. Compared with neighbouring Victoria, it lacks Victoria's 2025 criminal vilification offence but also lacks Victoria's coronial finding of police failure toward trans women; the two jurisdictions reach the same small positive deviation from different evidence.

National custody context: a national review estimates up to 400 trans and gender-diverse people are in prisons across the country, often inappropriately housed and at elevated risk of physical and sexual violence; four jurisdictions run explicit self-identification policies while others are unclear, and a 2026 report documents strip-searching practice and its disproportionate harms for trans, gender-diverse and indigenous prisoners across jurisdictions.
rewrites.localsOnly:
Health-capacity data: a 2022 government study found serious barriers for transgender and gender-diverse residents — a shortage of primary-care professionals and specialists with expertise in trans health, excessive wait times, delays from referrals and high costs associated with travel; the territory is described as the only jurisdiction without a comprehensive gender-focused health service, with one paediatric specialist carrying a waitlist of 20 young transgender people and demand rising 20-40 per cent a year.

Resident framing of the conversion-practices ban: amendments before passage followed arguments by religious schools and the local law society that the definition of conversion practice was too broad and vague.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes:
The 'no countervailing regional finding' assessment is qualified by the documented health-capacity gap for residents, which is the closest thing to a region-specific institutional finding in the dossier.
No visitor documents or border-screening practice specific to this territory is recorded in the dossier, beyond the documented strip-searching practice for people in custody.
